title: Correct SmCo precipitation methods locator and retain review lineage
body:
The new `data/records/samarium-cobalt-magnet-scrap.yaml` draft has a minor primary-source locator error in `mechanisms[id=samarium_precipitation_and_oxide_conversion].context`.

At the frozen working-state SHA-256 `b451f6a75dee9631629426aadc9d1fb157cdbb9502daca7c1029d63b26db628e`, the context cites Sections 2.3.2 and 3.3 for precipitation. In the complete [Nayak et al. original](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7807480/), Section 2.3.2 is **Solvent Extraction** and Section 2.3.3 is **Precipitation**. The detailed conditions also remain supported by Section 3.3. The curator reported this after freezing the draft; the coordinator independently checked the original section labels. The initial native independent review is being retained before correction.

Acceptance criteria:

- Correct the methods locator to Section 2.3.3 without silently changing the experimental conditions.
- Append a canonical EDIT history session and a distinct inline change event.
- Preserve the initial independent review and save a successor with the same stable finding key, exact predecessor link, and final record hash.
- Pass strict record validation, trusted-base history validation, the structured-review check, and the batch gates.

This issue concerns record traceability. The original paper's peroxide-recipe and supplementary mass-balance conflicts are separate unresolved source questions; fixing the locator does not resolve them or authorize an overall recovery yield.

Deduplication checked all 169 non-PR issues, open and closed, through the paginated API on 2026-10-14; no matching SmCo/DOI issue was found in that inventory.

title: Resolve contradictory MLCC leaching endpoints and sampling provenance in Masache-Romero 2025
body:
The new waste-multilayer-ceramic-capacitors record accepts only qualified abiotic mobilization from the characterized post-consumer computer-component feed. DOI https://doi.org/10.3390/molecules30214254 (Molecules 30:4254; complete original, 18 pages) contains unresolved quantitative conflicts:

- Section 2.2.2 gives ternary/glycerol Ni extraction of about 25%/6% at 24 h in one paragraph, matching Figure 2 and Conclusions, but the next paragraph gives 68%/16%.
- The abstract gives a maximum Fe extraction of 60%; Figure 3 and Conclusions indicate about 68% for the citric-acid binary solvent. Other Fe endpoints vary between prose and conclusion.
- Section 4.4 lists sampling at 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6 and 24 h; the figures include a 16 h point.
- Table 3 and Section 3.3 identify ternary viscosity as estimated, not experimentally measured. This must remain separate from measured extraction and energy performance.

The complete official PDF and XML were acquired and all claim-bearing graphics inspected. No corresponding correction was returned by the bounded DOI/title notice search; this is not an assertion that none exists. The record preserves these limits and does not import a reconciled percentage series.

Follow-up acceptance: locate a publisher correction or attributable original assay data defining the correct time-point/end-point values, feed denominator, sampling-volume correction, replicates and error bars. Reconcile each affected figure/prose claim explicitly; keep unknowns if no evidence resolves them. A different MLCC experiment does not resolve this original experiment's discrepancies. Any quantitative update needs new history and independent review. This is an open source clarification, not a defect requiring fabricated record measurements.

The coordinator also checked the relevant original text and claim-bearing figures/tables before filing. All-state paginated issue deduplication was performed on 2026-10-14. Related record-locator correction: #260; it does not resolve these source questions.

title: Resolve SmCo magnet-scrap peroxide recipe and supplementary samarium mass balance
body:
Nayak et al., Process Flowsheet Development for Separation of Sm, Co, Cu, and Fe from Magnet Scrap, ACS Omega 6:188–196, DOI https://doi.org/10.1021/acsomega.0c04132 (PMC7807480), supports qualified abiotic leaching and phase-characterized Sm products. Complete original XML/HTML, all 12 main figures and the four-page original supplement were acquired and inspected.

Two unresolved source issues prevent a transferable optimized recipe or accepted overall recovery percentage:

- Methods Section 2.3.1 specifies 5% v/v H2O2 for all leaches, but Conclusions states 1%. Main Table 2's additional 15% HCl/70°C/3 h arm cannot be assigned a single unqualified peroxide recipe.
- Supplement Table S3 lists 20 g scrap, 12.47 g Sm2O3 and 84.83% overall recovery. Main Section 3.1 gives 32.2% Sm in the feed, equivalent to 6.44 g input Sm. The printed pure-oxide product mass requires more Sm than this input inventory. The table also prints Sm2(CO4)3, unlike the oxalate assignment in Figure S1. Do not resolve these inconsistencies by inventing a different feed, yield denominator or purity.

Secondary process-recipe conflicts also remain: Section 3.4 alternates CaO/NaOH for iron precipitation; Cu stripping acid is expressed differently in text and Figure 7 caption. These have not been converted into an accepted precise integrated recipe. The record retains conditional source extraction values and qualitative phase-supported product formation without accepting the 84.83% overall value.

Follow-up acceptance: find a publisher correction or attributable experiment record reconciling reagent-stock basis, peroxide volume, starting batch/composition, liquor losses, precipitate masses, moisture/purity and the Sm2O3 mass. Provide a closed Sm inventory and explicit denominator before accepting an overall yield. Bound the source's Fig12 recycle/discharge proposal separately from actual experiments. Preserve old claims and add history plus independent review for any supported update. This source gap is separate from the minor record citation-locator correction.

The coordinator also checked the relevant original text and claim-bearing figures/tables before filing. All-state paginated issue deduplication was performed on 2026-10-14. Related record-locator correction: #260; it does not resolve these source questions.
